newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says still gearing for defector departure.
newsitem.headline: Manila says still gearing for defector departure.

text.p: Philippine officials said on Friday they were so fearful for the safety of North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop that he may have to take a detour to reach Seoul and what promises to be a fanfare welcome.

"The timing and the preparations are still being discussed for the exit of Hwang from the Philippines," Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon told reporters. He declined to say anything more, citing security reasons.
"Perhaps we are going to announce the transfer after Hwang arrives in South Korea. We want to make sure he has landed there. We really don't want take any risks in this game," he said.
A military source said one matter still being discussed by security experts was the safest route to fly Hwang to Seoul.

That may have to include a detour into Japanese airspace before heading to the South Korean capital, where foreign and local media have been invited to witness the arrival of the most senior official to flee the communist state, the source said.

Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue, defected in Beijing on February 12 and has been in the Philippines since March 18. But his whereabouts have been a secret because of fears that he may be a target of Pyongyang's hitmen.

Hwang's clandestine departure from the South Korean consular compound in Beijing and the shroud of secrecy over where he has stayed in the Philippines have triggered a rash of rumours -- but no real clues -- as to where he is.
The only official word on Hwang has been that he is in a safe place watching videotapes and eating Korean food.
On Thursday, a senior Seoul Foreign Ministry official said Hwang would arrive in South Korea early next week.
Asked by reporters if Hwang was debriefed while in the Philippines, Siazon said: "Certainly not. Not even by foreign elements."
